glossary-accessibility-desc: Principles and techniques to make mobile apps usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. Includes support for screen readers, voice navigation, and compliance with standards such as WCAG.
glossary-ai-desc: A field of computer science that develops systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as natural language processing, computer vision, smart assistants, and autonomous decision-making.
glossary-android-desc: Google's mobile operating system, the most widely used worldwide. Enables native app development mainly in Kotlin or Java, and provides access to a wide variety of devices and features.
glossary-appclips-desc: Lightweight fragments of iOS applications that allow users to quickly access a specific functionality without installing the full app, improving experience and conversion.
glossary-arkit-arcore-desc: Apple and Google frameworks for creating augmented reality experiences on mobile devices, allowing virtual objects to be overlaid on the real world and enabling immersive apps.
glossary-aso-desc: Strategies and techniques to improve the visibility and downloads of an app in mobile app stores such as the App Store and Google Play.
glossary-contentmanager-desc: A system that allows you to add, modify, and delete content from an app or website without advanced technical knowledge. In mobile, it is often integrated with backend services or headless CMS platforms.
glossary-crossplatform-desc: Technologies and frameworks that allow you to develop a single app that works on multiple mobile operating systems, optimizing resources and development time (e.g., Flutter, React Native, Kotlin Multiplatform).
glossary-flutter-desc: Google's framework for creating mobile, web, and desktop applications from a single codebase using the Dart language. Enables high-performance apps with a consistent visual interface across multiple platforms.
glossary-html5css3-desc: Core languages for web and hybrid app development, although their use in mobile has declined in favor of native and cross-platform frameworks. Still useful for prototypes and simple apps.
glossary-ios-desc: Apple's operating system for iPhone and iPad. Known for its closed ecosystem, high performance, security, and access to the latest innovations in mobile hardware and software.
glossary-jetpackcompose-desc: Google's framework for building user interfaces declaratively on Android. Simplifies the development and maintenance of mobile apps with a modern, reactive approach.
glossary-kotlinmp-desc: A development framework that allows sharing business logic between mobile applications (Android and iOS) using the Kotlin language. Facilitates efficient cross-platform app development while maintaining native interfaces.
glossary-mcp-desc: Platforms that facilitate the development, deployment, and management of mobile applications in the cloud, enabling scalability, service integration, and data synchronization between devices and servers.
glossary-ml-desc: A discipline of artificial intelligence that enables mobile apps to learn from data and improve their performance over time, applying algorithms for pattern recognition, predictions, and task automation.
glossary-pwa-desc: Progressive web applications that offer an experience similar to a native app, including offline access, push notifications, and home screen access, combining the best of web and mobile.
glossary-react-desc: JavaScript library for building user interfaces. In mobile, React Native stands out, allowing you to create native apps for iOS and Android from a single codebase, combining performance and flexibility.
glossary-reactnative-desc: Facebook's framework based on React that allows you to create native mobile applications for iOS and Android from a single JavaScript codebase, combining native performance and agile development.
glossary-rust-desc: A modern, safe, and efficient programming language, increasingly used in the development of mobile components and embedded systems for its performance and reliability.
glossary-seo-desc: A set of techniques to improve the visibility of a website or app in search engines. In mobile, it is mainly applied to progressive web apps (PWAs) and to the optimization of app store listings (ASO).
glossary-swiftui-desc: Apple's declarative framework for creating user interfaces on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and VisionOS. Enables fast and efficient development of modern apps with less code and reactive views.
glossary-vibecoding-desc: An emerging approach to software development that prioritizes developer experience, real-time collaboration, and the integration of smart tools, enhancing creativity and efficiency in mobile teams.
glossary-visionos-desc: Apple's operating system for the Vision Pro device, focused on spatial computing and augmented reality experiences. Enables the creation of immersive 3D apps and new forms of interaction.
glossary-wordpress-desc: Popular platform for web content management, which can also be integrated with mobile apps via APIs to display or manage information.
glossary-xcode-desc: Apple's official development environment for creating native applications on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and VisionOS, using languages such as Swift and Objective-C.

Users can import their YouTube playlists into MixMasterTube and make them public for others to use or create new ones from the website. It also allows crossfading videos to facilitate mixing.

novoypedo-description-1: App designed and developed by us that simulates a breathalyzer. The user must enter the number of drinks consumed and the time frame, and the app calculates an approximate blood alcohol level based on these indicators and the user's weight.
novoypedo-description-2: The unique feature compared to other breathalyzers available on the App Store is that it is the only one where, to display the result, you have to blow, emulating with the iPhone the same action as with a real device.
novoypedo-description-3: The realism of this emulator is reflected in its results: The app has been translated into more than six languages and has appeared several times as one of the top ten most downloaded apps. There are currently two versions available, one free and one paid.

retropong-context: We decided to participate in an international contest organized by Atari to develop the new version of the Pong game for iOS devices. More than 100 participants entered the contest, we passed a first selection and then a second. In the final phase, we were chosen as finalists! Being a finalist ensures the publication of the game under the Atari brand.
retropong-development: We are currently finishing the last specifications of the game, we hope to have it available as soon as possible so you can enjoy it from the App Store.
retropong-game: The game has been developed for both iPhone and iPad. We aimed to offer the user the best Pong experience, so in addition to one or two player modes, the iPad version allows up to three or four players simultaneously.
retropong-modes: The game is divided into three separate modes: story mode, which allows you to progress through different levels; battle mode, where you can play remotely with other players; and multiplayer mode, which allows up to four people to play on the same screen.
retropong-video-desc: You can watch the promotional video we made to introduce the game. The video shows both the iPhone and iPad versions.
scrush-app-1: We wanted to create an intuitive and very visual app for household savings. On startup, the user can choose between two styles: cicada (one-time savings) and ant (regular savings). The app manages income and expenses for different months, shows information grouped by restaurants, phone, rent, etc., calculates recommended savings, and allows you to adjust the difficulty level to save more or less.
scrush-app-2: The user is responsible for trying to keep savings within the parameters they have chosen, and when they exceed any, a warning is sent.
scrush-app-3: To help the user save more easily, different discount coupons are offered based on their most common expenses, as well as banking products that may be useful. If you spend a lot on clothes, you will see discounts from clothing brands, you may be recommended offers or plans to help reduce your phone bill, etc. These offers can also be viewed on a map and via GPS.
scrush-app-4: When starting, the app asks for a code provided by the bank to access account movements.
scrush-context-1: We decided to participate in the FinAppsParty app development marathon organized by bdigitalapps and La Caixa. In 24 hours, a financial app for smartphones had to be developed. In addition to programming, we developed the initial idea, created the design templates, and even made a presentation video. More than 40 teams from several countries participated, but unfortunately, we were not among the winners this time, although we gained great experience.
scrush-context-2: Our team consisted of designer David Pareja and our PegPeg programmer.
scrush-video-desc: You can watch the promotional video we made at the end of the marathon to present our app.

webapps-alt: Cross-platform application development with modern frameworks
webapps-choosing-description: The selection of a cross-platform development framework depends on various factors including project requirements, target audience, performance needs, and development timeline. Each approach offers unique advantages:
webapps-description-1: Flutter represents Google's innovative UI toolkit for crafting beautiful, natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase. With Flutter, developers can create high-performance apps that feel natural on different platforms while maintaining a consistent brand experience. The framework offers hot reload for quick development cycles and a rich set of customizable widgets for building native interfaces.
webapps-description-2: React Native enables developers to build mobile applications using JavaScript and React. This framework, maintained by Facebook, allows for efficient development of truly native apps for both iOS and Android platforms. Its key advantage lies in the ability to share up to 90% of code between platforms while still delivering native performance and look-and-feel.
webapps-description-3: We also have extensive experience in developing websites especially oriented to mobile devices and microsites.
webapps-flutter-advantage: Flutter: Ideal for highly customized UIs and applications requiring smooth animations
webapps-pwa-advantage: PWAs: Excellent for web-first applications requiring broad reach and offline capabilities
webapps-react-advantage: React Native: Perfect for projects needing quick development cycles and good native integration
webapps-xamarin-advantage: Kotlin Multiplatform: Excellent for teams wanting to share business logic while maintaining native UI development
webapps-xamarin-description: Kotlin Multiplatform enables developers to share business logic across iOS and Android while keeping native UI development. It provides excellent interoperability with existing iOS and Android codebases, allowing teams to gradually adopt cross-platform development. The framework offers great performance and native feel while reducing code duplication.
